July 28, 2026

Thirsty?

 

Scripture: “The woman said to him, ‘Sir, you have nothing to draw water with, and the well is deep. Where do you get that living water? Are you greater than our father Jacob? He gave us the well and drank from it himself, as did his sons and his livestock.’ Jesus said to her, ‘Everyone who drinks of this water will be thirsty again, but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never be thirsty again. The water that I will give him will become in him a spring of water welling up to eternal life.’ The woman said to him, ‘Sir, give me this water, so that I will not be thirsty or have to come here to draw water.’” — John 4:11–15

 

Thought: The Samaritan woman was still thinking about the well, but Jesus was talking about her soul. She looked at Him and asked how He could possibly give living water. He had no bucket, and the well was deep. Jesus replies, “Everyone who drinks some of this water will be thirsty again.”

 

That statement reaches far beyond Jacob’s well into our very hearts… Jesus is saying...

 

"Drink from success, and you will thirst again."

"Drink from money, and you will thirst again."

"Drink from approval, pleasure, recognition, possessions, or relationships, and eventually you will thirst again."

 

Every earthly well has a limit. Every achievement becomes yesterday’s win. Every new purchase loses its shine. Every applause grows quiet. Every person we love will eventually disappoint us if we ask them to carry the weight of our souls.

 

The problem is not that these things are bad. Many of them are gifts from God. The problem begins when we ask good gifts to become gods. We keep returning to wells that cannot satisfy because we are asking created things to do what only the Creator can do.

 

Jesus offers something entirely different… “Whoever drinks some of the water that I will give him will never be thirsty again.” Jesus does not simply offer a better version of what the world gives. He offers Himself. The world says, “Keep coming back.” Jesus says, “I will put a fountain within you.”

 

The grace, forgiveness, peace, and eternal life Jesus gives are not temporary relief. He says His water becomes “a fountain of water springing up to eternal life.”

 

The problem is not that we have desires. The problem is that we often take good desires to the wrong wells.

 

We want significance, so we chase success.

We want security, so we chase money.

We want to be loved, so we make another person responsible for our worth.

We want peace, so we numb ourselves with comfort and entertainment.

We want to know that we matter, so we chase recognition.

 

And we wonder why we are still thirsty? Our repeated thirst is trying to tell us something. We have cravings that this world can never satisfy. The ache beneath your ambition, your approval-seeking, your restlessness, and your desire for more is pointing beyond itself.

 

Your soul was made for God. Augustine famously wrote that our hearts are restless until they find their rest in Him.

 

That is exactly what Jesus is showing the woman. She came to the well because she needed water. She was about to discover that her deepest need was standing in front of her.

 

The same is true for us. You can keep lowering the bucket into the same old wells. Or you can receive what Jesus alone can give. Every well apart from Him will leave you thirsty again.

 

Reflect: What earthly well do you return to when you feel empty? What are you asking success, money, relationships, or approval to provide that only Jesus can give?

 

Right Next Step: Name one “well” you have been expecting to satisfy you. Bring that desire honestly to Christ today and ask Him to teach you to find your deepest satisfaction in Him.

 

Prayer: “Father, forgive me for returning to wells that cannot satisfy. I have looked to success, approval, comfort, relationships, and possessions to give me what only You can provide. Turn my heart toward Jesus. Give me the living water of Your grace and teach me to find my deepest joy and satisfaction in Him. In Jesus’ name, amen.”
